      Data sources

        Methodology

        Periods
        Each section shows its own period. Economic impact is calendar 2025 vs. 2024; quarterly visitor data is Q2 2026 vs. Q2 2025; hotel forecasts run to 2030; CoStar hotel data is trailing 12 months or year to date through Aug. 2026; Symphony data covers the dates on each page.
        Forecasts
        Values marked F or "forecast" are third-party projections (Tourism Economics, LARC, CoStar) and can change with each edition.
        BI calculations
        Spending per visitor, food and beverage shares, commute shares, bus service counts and the one-more-night scenarios are calculated by Visit Anaheim BI from the published figures. They are labeled where used.
        One more night
        Headline: 2025 lodging spending ($1.72B) ÷ weighted average stay (2.17 days) = about $794M for one more night. Alternatives: overnight visitors adding a day at average daily spending ($1.02B); every visitor adding a day ($3.15B, upper bound).
        Two hotel bases
        LARC market tables use CoStar's Anaheim market. Visit Anaheim hotel set tables use the Anaheim and Garden Grove sets. CoStar's Disneyland submarket is a separate CoStar geography. Do not compare these bases directly.
        Symphony (Azira)
        Mobile location samples. Overnight and new-visitor shares count visitors who stayed 4+ hours, are not commuters and live 50+ miles away.

        Definitions

        Revenue per available room
        Room revenue divided by rooms available (RevPAR).
        Average nightly rate
        Room revenue divided by rooms sold (ADR).
        Visitor
        Someone who stayed overnight or traveled more than 50 miles to the destination (Tourism Economics).
        Total economic impact
        Direct visitor spending plus supply-chain (indirect) and income (induced) effects.
        Jobs supported
        Full- and part-time jobs, including proprietors (Bureau of Economic Analysis definition).
        Visits per 1,000 impressions
        Observed visits after ad exposure divided by measurable impressions, times 1,000.
        TID
        TID: the Anaheim Tourism Improvement District that funds incentive buydowns.
